missing_requirements.description: The promised fail-closed component/type/finiteness validation is incomplete for standard NumPy ndarray subclasses. MaskedArray inputs can pass validation while hiding nonfinite underlying coordinates or leaving masked hand coordinates unnormalized, and matrix pose inputs escape as IndexError rather than a clear ValueError. See L01.

logic_errors.title: Accepted semantic ndarray subclasses bypass fail-closed validation and can silently corrupt packed features
logic_errors.description: The isinstance(array, np.ndarray) check admits np.ma.MaskedArray and np.matrix. Their arithmetic/indexing semantics are not those assumed by the normalization code. For MaskedArray, np.isfinite(array).all() ignores masked entries; astype preserves the subclass; masked coordinates are not normalized by the assignments; concatenation drops their missingness while retaining underlying unnormalized data. A partially masked hand can therefore become an apparently complete observation with a hand-present mask of 1. A masked NaN in an unselected pose point is also accepted despite the all-components-finite requirement. For matrix pose input, shoulder_delta remains shape (1,2), so shoulder_delta[1] at line 50 raises IndexError. The normal SDK conversion currently returns ordinary ndarrays, but pack_frame is itself the public shared input-validation boundary and does not reject these other NumPy types.
observed_evidence: Minimal ordinary pose fixture: pose=np.zeros((33,4)); pose[11]=[0,0,0,1]; pose[12]=[2,0,0,1]; left_hand=np.ones((21,3)); right_hand=None. Its ordinary ndarray hand has normalized packed[3]=0.0.

Wrapping that hand with np.ma.array(..., mask=False), then setting hand.mask[1,0]=True, passes validation and returns MaskedArray shape (153,) with packed[3]=1.0 (the raw, unnormalized X), rather than rejecting the unsupported partial observation; masks are [1.0,0.0,1.0].

Wrapping the pose with np.ma.array(..., mask=False), setting pose.data[0,0]=np.nan and pose.mask[0,0]=True, makes np.isfinite(pose.data).all() False but np.isfinite(pose).all() True; pack_frame returns pose-usable mask 1.0 instead of raising ValueError.
Replacing the fixture pose with np.asmatrix(pose) raises IndexError: index 1 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 1, at features.py:50.

Executed an additional in-memory unittest harness for exactly these three boundaries with the approved Python, TMPDIR and -E -B flags: exit 1, Ran 3 tests, FAILED (failures=2, errors=1). This was not a rerun of the existing 38-test suite. No fixture files, native detectors, models, cameras or data sources were used.
logic_errors.minimal_reproducer:
import dataclasses
import numpy as np
from training.holistic_migration.features import RawFrame, pack_frame
p = np.zeros((33, 4), dtype=np.float64)
p[11] = [0, 0, 0, 1]
p[12] = [2, 0, 0, 1]
f = RawFrame(0, p, np.ones((21, 3)), None)
h = np.ma.array(f.left_hand, mask=False, copy=True)
h.mask[1, 0] = True
print(pack_frame(f)[3], pack_frame(dataclasses.replace(f, left_hand=h))[3])
q = np.ma.array(p, mask=False, copy=True)
q.data[0, 0] = np.nan
q.mask[0, 0] = True
print(pack_frame(dataclasses.replace(f, pose=q))[152])
pack_frame(dataclasses.replace(f, pose=np.asmatrix(p)))
logic_errors.expected_behavior: Reject masked/otherwise unsupported semantic array types with a component-specific ValueError before normalization; any deliberately supported ndarray subclass must preserve plain-array normalization and must not hide nonfinite or missing observations. Do not return apparently observed raw coordinates or leak incidental indexing errors.
logic_errors.recommended_change: Make the accepted array semantics explicit at the shared boundary: reject semantic subclasses such as MaskedArray/matrix, or intentionally support safe subclasses through validated plain-ndarray copies without discarding masking or nonfinite evidence. Add covering tests for partially masked hands, masked nonfinite pose values, and matrix pose input. No source changes were made by this review.
